text:
sam: Heads-up — after the RBAC tweak we pushed to ingest IAM role yesterday, a few decrypts are failing in prod. Lambda logs show AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt when running the envelope unwrap.
priya: Ugh. Which principal is showing in the KMS denial?
sam: Log shows: 
```
Request failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
```
priya: That looks like an assumed-role principal — did we change the trust or session policy?
alex: FYI I pushed the small RBAC change to block broad kms:* on non-prod roles yesterday (intended for safety). Could have overlapped with the ingest-role policy.
michael: Also check KMS KeyPolicy. If the key has a strict policy requiring explicit principal ARNs, an assumed-role ARN might not match unless the role is allowed. We saw similar when we enabled key rotation for that CMK.
irene: Quick checklist: (1) cloudtrail for Decrypt events, (2) check grants (active grants may still allow decrypt), (3) verify the exact principal in key policy.
cloudtrail-bot: New event: AWSKMS.Decrypt — Status: AccessDenied — CallerIdentity: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/ingest-role/session — EventTime: 2026-03-18T09:14:32Z
priya: Can someone paste the key policy and the role inline policy? If there's a session policy applied at assume-role time, it can remove kms:Decrypt permission even if role has it.
sam: Role inline policy excerpt: 
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```
alex: Key policy excerpt (sanitized): 
```
{
  "Statement": [
    {"Sid": "AllowAccountAdmins", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root"}, "Action": "kms:*", "Effect": "Allow"},
    {"Sid": "AllowServiceUsingKey", "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role"}, "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"], "Effect": "Allow"}
  ]
}
```
priya: Hmm — key policy allows the role ARN, but CloudTrail shows assumed-role session ARN. That should be allowed, but if the assume-role call included a SessionPolicy that removed kms:Decrypt, it will be denied. Any assume-role calls with session-policy params?
michael: We do apply session tags/policies in the token broker for some cross-account flows. Also note: if the CMK was rotated and a grant was retired, there may be an active grant mismatch. Check ListGrants output.
alex: Running quick commands: 
```
aws sts get-caller-identity --output text
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/ingest-cmk
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/ingest-cmk
```
sam: I ran list-grants — it returned one grant but Status shows GRANT_PENDING_RETIREMENT (we rotated and the retire didn't fully propagate). Could be a propagation window.
irene: If a grant is pending retirement and key policy uses grants to allow decrypt for an assumed role, you can see transient denies. Also check if grant tokens were used during encryption (client-side) — if data was encrypted under a grant token, Decrypt needs the same grant or for the grant to still be active.
priya: For immediate mitigation — can we either (A) add the sts assumed principal ARN pattern to the key policy wildcard (e.g., arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/*) or (B) create a short-lived explicit grant for the ingest-role to allow kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey without waiting for rotation propagation? Thoughts?
michael: Option B is lower blast radius and faster. I'll create a grant with retiring allowed and tag it with incident id. If that fixes it, we can roll back and then re-evaluate the rotation workflow.
alex: Agreed. Also let's capture why the session policy changed — CI/CD RBAC change merged yesterday (PR #478). Sam, can you roll that back on a branch and we can test assume-role locally with a session policy to reproduce?
sam: On it. I'll simulate assume with and without session policy: 
```
aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role --role-session-name test --policy file://restrict.json
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.blob --key-id alias/ingest-cmk
```
priya: Also please check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt events around rotation time to confirm timing. If we rotated the CMK just before RBAC change, that explains the race.
irene: Logging action item: ensure CloudTrail sends Decrypt events to our SIEM and create an alert for repeated AccessDenied on kms:Decrypt from same role. I'll open a ticket.
cloudtrail-bot: Alert created: SEC-3124 — Repeated KMS AccessDenied for ingest-role — investigators: security oncall
priya: Good. Michael — ping when grant exists and we'll try a canary decrypt.
michael: Grant created: grantId: 9a1b2c3d-xyz — added kms:Decrypt to granteePrincipal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ingest-role — testing now.
sam: Canary run succeeded, lambda decrypts now OK. Please keep grant until we resolve rotation flow.
priya: Next steps: (1) revert/adjust RBAC PR to avoid removing kms:Decrypt from session policy, (2) verify rotation workflow doesn't retire grants mid-flight, (3) tighten key policy but include assumed-role ARN pattern if needed, (4) add alert.
irene: I'll file follow-ups and assign owners. Thanks all :thumbsup:
